newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle markets remain quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle markets remain quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained quiet late Wednesday morning with a few bids of $65.00 per cwt reported from Kansas to Texas, feedlot sources said.
"They (packers) will bid that on about anything you have got," said an Oklahoma cattle feeder.
Most showlists were depleted during the moderate to active trading Tuesday at $66.00, sources said.
Some feedlot managers said they would consider the $65.00 bids for lower-grading cattle because they need the pen space for incoming feeder cattle.

Placements have slowed somewhat from November's active pace, but some feedlot sources said they continue to receive feeder cattle off wheat pastures. An Oklahoma manager said it was difficult to lock in a profitable hedge on newly-placed cattle.
Many feedlot managers said their lots are full or nearly full.
